epic.title: cleanup-g-crew-tier
epic.intent_and_why: A crew's model tier was never a deliberate choice at the seam where every dispatch actually passes through -- run_crew.py's build_crew_argv accepted a None model silently, and reasoning_effort was recorded but never forwarded to the launcher. This makes the choice explicit and mandatory.

definition_of_done: run_crew.py refuses a fresh or relaunched crew dispatch that names no --model, fail closed, no invented default.
reasoning_effort is forwarded as the launcher's real --effort flag on the cli backend, both dispatch and resume.
crew-dispatch.md doctrine names the handoff's Suggested Model Tier field as the thing a Commander resolves --model from.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Independent reviewer APPROVE on the code gate; red/green test evidence for the doctrine gate; full clean-env suite green modulo an explicitly reported caller-list residue; main baseline re-measured at gate time.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Red/green tests for the refusal, the --effort forwarding (both call sites), and the doctrine connection; a mechanically-derived caller-list enumeration.
good_enough.appetite: One working session, Sonnet 5 tier, mechanical change with pre-ruled direction.

hard_constraints: Fenced: scripts/checklist_engine.py, scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py, scripts/spine_lifecycle.py and their tests (lane F live)
Fenced: COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json, LAUNCH_ORDER.template.md, fleet-doctrine.md, skills/_shared/**, install_constellation.py (queued #610)
No crew's effective tier may change as a side effect (decision:do-not-change-what-anything-runs-at)
#607's parent-lease-heartbeat thread ordering must survive unchanged
fixed_decisions: relaunch requires explicit --model, no inherit-from-abandoned-entry fallback (Commander ruling, within Inherited Latitude)

issues.title: Crew model tier is inherited or silently absent, never a deliberate choice
issues.desired_outcome: run_crew.py refuses a tierless fresh/relaunch dispatch; reasoning_effort reaches --effort; doctrine names the connection.
issues.useful_now: Stops the fleet from reproducing the pre-mission defect (lane A/E baselines showed dispatched crews silently falling back to the machine default) inside its own fix.
issues.appetite: Two crew-dispatch gates (g1: implement/review/integrate) plus one reasoning gate (g2: doctrine) plus one reasoning gate (g3: verify).
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: MandatoryModelTests (6 new tests) + 4 flipped --effort tests + doctrine red/green test; both directions proven (refusal fires on fresh/relaunch, does not fire on resume/bare-abandon).
issues.implementation_latitude: Refusal wording/exit code; exact relaunch semantics; whether the doctrine field becomes machine-read or stays prose (chose: stays prose, per the pre-ruling's own settle guidance).
hard_constraints_no_gos: No existing dispatch's effective tier may change.

wave_forecast.outcome: The two out-of-owned-files test failures (tests/test_crew_worktree_cwd.py, tests/test_work_id_nesting.py) get a mechanical model= reconciliation, either as this mission's own immediate follow-up or via the filed triage candidate.
wave_forecast.why_likely: It is the same one-line-per-call-site pattern already applied ~27 times in tests/test_crew_launcher.py this run; no design question remains.
entry_conditions: Admiral or a follow-up dispatch picks up triage candidate tc1

uncertainty_register.unknown: Whether any dispatch caller outside this repo's own test suite (e.g. a consuming project's own tooling) constructs a CrewSpec with no model and would now be refused.
uncertainty_register.affects: Blast radius of decision:refuse-a-tierless-dispatch beyond this repo
uncertainty_register.settle_by: Observed in the field the first time a consuming project's own automation calls run_crew.py without --model
uncertainty_register.current_evidence: grep of the live tree in this repo found zero non-test-file callers outside scripts/run_crew.py itself; not evidence about other repos.
uncertainty_register.next_probe: Not this run's scope -- run_crew.py is a bundled skill script, not a published library with an external changelog.

parked_possibilities: A controlled vocabulary or explicit --model pointer inside the handoff templates themselves (both plan candidates and the cold critic left this as a named untaken road, per the pre-ruling's settle guidance preferring prose over a parser).

completed_outcomes.outcome: CrewSpec.__post_init__ refuses a falsy model (fresh/relaunch only, structurally exempting resume/bare-abandon); build_crew_argv forwards reasoning_effort as --effort on both CliBackend.dispatch and .resume; crew-dispatch.md names the connection. Committed as part of this run's branch.
completed_outcomes.evidence: MandatoryModelTests (6 tests, both directions: refusal fires and does not fire); 4 flipped --effort forwarding tests; test_crew_dispatch_doctrine.py (2 tests, red-then-green, pasted in notes-g.md); independent reviewer APPROVE with full re-derivation of every close criterion, not trust.

wave_evidence.expected: CrewLaunchError on missing model; success + entry['model'] set when given.

wave_evidence.observed: test_reasoning_effort_is_recorded_and_forwarded_as_effort_flag, test_cli_resume_reads_reasoning_effort_from_registry, test_legacy_resume_without_reasoning_effort_does_not_crash all pass, argv index/value asserted not just membership.

discrepancies.signal: A first scratch-clone baseline measurement produced a false MapTreeFreshnessTests failure because the clone directory was named g3-main-baseline instead of constellation-skills -- map/INDEX.md's generated header bakes in the repo directory name.
discrepancies.affects: Any future Commander's baseline-remeasurement method, not this lane's own correctness
discrepancies.evidence: Re-cloned into a correctly-named directory (/tmp/g3-baseline-root/constellation-skills); the failure disappeared, 3163 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed.
discrepancies.reason: A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed, and the inverse held here too -- a check that fails on a harmless naming artifact reads as a real regression unless caught. Not this lane's file ownership to fix (map_orient.py/code_map are outside file ownership); noted for triage rather than filed as an issue by this run.
